🔍 A.I. Search Startup's Value Balloons Past A Small Nation's Budget; Now Too Big To Actually Answer Your Question

SILICON VALLEY — reported after a very long 'thinking…' spinner

MARKETS — An AI search company's valuation reportedly leapt from around $20 billion last year toward the stratosphere, with revenue topping $750 million as it pushes beyond mere search into "agents" that handle complex professional tasks — meaning it has graduated from answering your questions to confidently doing your job.

"We're redefining how people find information," the company said, of a service now worth more than several countries and most human feelings. Analysts note the thesis is simple: if you own the box everyone types their questions into, you can eventually charge for the answers, the follow-ups, and possibly the silence in between.

REGULATION — New Zealand advanced legislation to keep young users off certain platforms, joining a global wave of age-ban laws — a well-meaning effort destined to be defeated, as always, within minutes, by a teenager and a birth year ending in a suspiciously round number.

🐌 New A.I. Models Deliberately Think Slower To Be Smarter; Finally, A Computer That Says 'Let Me Get Back To You'

THE DATA CENTER — reported during a long, thoughtful pause

MODELS — The latest frontier models increasingly trade raw speed for accuracy, taking extra time to "reason" before answering — meaning that, after decades of demanding faster computers, we have finally built one that thoughtfully asks for a minute.

"Slower is smarter," researchers explained, of models that now pause, ponder, and double-check like a wise elder instead of blurting out the first thing that comes to mind. Users report the answers are markedly better and the waiting markedly worse, proving once again you cannot have everything — even from a machine that cost a billion dollars.
